units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5:1:4">Y. Succ. V, beg. 55ᵃ</cite> <he>הי לך מצה</he> here is unleavened bread for thee. Combined <cite ref="E00400"><he>הֵילָךְ</he></cite>.
B. Mets. 4ᵃ I owe thee only fifty Zuz, וה׳ and here they are.—Hence (law) helakh, the instantaneous delivery of the amount confessed, while the creditor claims a larger amount.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 4a">Ib.</cite> <he>ה׳ פטור וכ׳</he> if one delivers one portion of the claim (says, ‘here it is’), he is exempt from taking an oath (as one who confesses a part of a claimed debt otherwise must do); a. fr.

senses.gloss: (interrog.) which? Ḥull. 14ᵃ הי ר׳ יהודה which R. Judah, i.e. to which opinion of R. J. do you allude? Sabb. 9ᵇ הי סמוך וכ׳ which ‘near Minḥah’ is meant in the Mishnah?—
units: <cite ref="Chullin 49b:14">Ḥull. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>הי מינייהו</he> which of them (eventually closes up a hole in the entrails); a. fr.

senses.gloss: where? Ber. 31ᵃ הי תורה וכ׳ where is the law, and where the good deeds to protect us?—
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 5:23">Targ. Y. Deut. V, 23</cite>, v. <cite ref="D00918"><he>דֵּן</he></cite>.—<he>הי דינו</he>, v. <cite ref="E00369"><he>הַיְידְּנוּ</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 32:41">Targ. Y. I Deut. XXXII, 41</cite> <he>הֵיא ברק</he> (not <cite ref="E00331"><he>הִיא</he></cite>) as lightning. Mostly <he>הי כ־</he>; comb. <cite ref="E00373"><he>היכ־</he></cite>.
